Date: 2026-05-01T09:12:00-04:00
Subject: Supply chain inventory + SOC2/CAIQ request

Marcus —

Thanks for taking this. As part of Evergreen’s vendor security review we’re consolidating subprocessor mappings and CAIQ/SIG evidence. Can you please provide the following by next Wednesday (5/6):

- A canonical subprocessor inventory (CSV) with: vendor name, service provided, data types processed (PII/PD/Logs), country of processing, first onboarded date, and termination notice period.
- A redacted copy or summary of your most recent SOC 2 report (if you cannot share the full report, a one-page summary of scope and controls is fine).
- Completed CAIQ/consensus SIG responses or a link to them.
- Any DSP/DPA clauses that reference subprocessors and data residency options (especially for EU data).

Attached is our VendorChecklist_v2.xlsx — we try to map fields to that template to speed review. If you expect any of the items to take longer, please let me know so we can adjust the review window.

Best,
Tom Harris
Senior Information Security Manager
Evergreen Health

Hi Tom / Evergreen team —

Attached is the canonical subprocessor inventory (subprocessors_inventory_20260504.csv) and our redacted SOC 2 summary (SOC2_summary_redacted.pdf). I’ve also attached our CAIQ responses (CAIQ_responses_20260504.pdf). Below is a short mapping highlighting the most common subprocessors and where they process data — the full CSV has the columns requested in your checklist.

Top-level subprocessors (excerpt):
- Amazon Web Services (AWS): compute, storage, KMS (control plane in us-east-1 and eu-west-1 depending on customer routing). Data types: application telemetry, logs (PD), model artifacts. Onboarded: 2019-06-12. Termination notice: 30 days for contractual termination; longer for retained logs by agreement.
- Datadog, Inc.: monitoring & metrics. Data types: metrics & application logs (non-PII by default). Onboarded: 2020-03-01. Termination notice: 30 days.
- Sentry, Inc.: error reporting. Data types: exception traces (may include PD if present in stack traces). Onboarded: 2021-08-15.
- HashiCorp (Vault): secrets management for hosted control plane ops; customer-managed Vault options for Private deployments. Onboarded: 2022-02-11.
- VectorAI (example ML vendor): model optimization & quantization pipeline (model artifacts only). Onboarded: 2024-11-05.

EU residency: entries in the CSV are flagged with the processing location. For hosted EU traffic we route through eu-west-1 by default; you’ll see explicit eu entries in the CSV exported column "processing_region".

SOC 2 summary notes (high level):
- Scope: infrastructure and control plane for hosted inference API; excludes customer-managed private deployments unless contractually in scope.
- Last audit: 2025-12. Auditor: ClearPath Audit LLP. No exceptions that affect data residency controls.
- Redaction: we removed auditor contact details and customer names from the attached summary per our standard sharing practice. We can provide a sealed SOC 2 under NDA if you require it.

CAIQ responses: the attached PDF maps control families to our internal evidence references. If Evergreen prefers the SIG questionnaire instead, we can export the same answers in that format within 24 hours.

Attachments: subprocessors_inventory_20260504.csv, SOC2_summary_redacted.pdf, CAIQ_responses_20260504.pdf

Let me know if you want a call to walk through the CSV — happy to run through specific rows.

Thanks,
Naomi Feldman
Head of Compliance — Redwood Inference

Naomi / Marcus —

Appreciate the fast turnaround and the CSV. A couple of follow-ups after a quick pass:

1) Can you confirm which subprocessors have servers physically located in the EU (not just EU endpoints)? The CSV flags "eu-west-1" for some entries but we need confirmation of physical processing for PHI/PD purposes.
2) Do any subprocessors use HSMs (CloudHSM or similar) for key material used in production? If yes, which ones and where are HSMs located?
3) Please paste the exact DPA subsection that describes Redwood’s ability to sub-contract processing (we only need the text snippet for legal review).

If it helps, we can take the SOC 2 summary under NDA and then request the sealed report. Would you prefer an NDA or is the redacted summary sufficient to proceed to legal review?

Thanks —
Tom

Tom —

Quick answers inline to your three points below and an attached short summary for EU-specific subprocessors (subprocessor_eu_summary.txt).

1) EU physical processing: confirmed subprocessors with EU-resident physical processing are AWS (eu-west-1 & eu-central-1 availability zones), Datadog EU endpoints (managed in eu-west-1), and our EU model ops partner (VectorAI) which runs compute in Frankfurt. The CSV has rows with exact footprint and "processing_country" column populated; see rows 12-18 for the EU entries.

2) HSM usage: we use AWS CloudHSM for key material in our hosted control plane in production (CloudHSM clusters in us-east-1 and eu-west-1). For Private deployments customers may opt to use their own HSMs or KMS. HashiCorp Vault is used for secrets orchestration but Vault itself is backed by CloudHSM in the hosted config.

3) DPA excerpt (exact subsection): "Redwood Inference may engage subprocessors to perform certain processing activities on behalf of the Customer. Redwood remains responsible for such subprocessors’ performance and shall impose data protection obligations equivalent to those in this Agreement. A list of subprocessors and processing locations is maintained and provided upon request; customers may request a DPA addendum to restrict specific subprocessors or regions for Private deployments."

NDA: the redacted SOC2 summary is acceptable for initial legal review; if Evergreen requires the sealed SOC2 we’ll coordinate an NDA and controlled delivery.

If you’d like, I can schedule a 30-minute call with Naomi and Priyom tomorrow to walk through the CSV.

Best,
